meta.subject: English
meta.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft
meta.title: Rebuild the Sentence: Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses not only...but also while keeping the subject in place and giving each half one simple-past active verb?
choices: Not only did the interns catalog every sample, but they also recorded each test result carefully.
The interns not only cataloged and recorded every sample but also filed each test result carefully.
The interns not only cataloged every sample but also recorded each test result carefully.
The interns not only cataloged every sample but also were recording each test result carefully.
questions.explanation: This construction keeps the interns as the subject and uses one active simple-past verb in each half, so the two actions remain parallel.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The coach would rather revising the plan than presenting it. Which revision uses parallel infinitives after would rather?
choices: The coach would rather revise the plan than present it.
The coach would rather to revise the plan than present it.
The coach would rather revise the plan than to present it.
The coach would rather revising the plan than present it.
questions.explanation: Would rather is followed by the parallel infinitives revise and present, which clearly express the coach's preference.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The bicycle repair shop stays open until six. It is located on Pine Street. Which revision correctly places a nonrestrictive relative clause immediately after its antecedent to add the location as extra information?
choices: The bicycle repair shop stays open until six, which is located on Pine Street.
The bicycle repair shop on Pine Street stays open until six.
The bicycle repair shop, which is located on Pine Street, stays open until six.
The bicycle repair shop, located on Pine Street, stays open until six.
questions.explanation: The nonrestrictive relative clause which is located on Pine Street directly follows and modifies bicycle repair shop and is correctly set off by commas.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision uses one introductory dependent clause followed by one independent clause?
choices: The runners completed the relay before dusk, although the rain delayed the start.
Although the rain delayed the start, the runners completed the relay before dusk.
The rain delayed the start, and the runners completed the relay before dusk.
Although the rain delayed the start, and because the team wanted to win, they completed the relay.
questions.explanation: The revision places one dependent although-clause before one independent clause, the structure the prompt asks for.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses a nonrestrictive appositive to identify Ms. Alvarez?
choices: Ms. Alvarez, our science teacher introduced the visiting speakers.
Ms. Alvarez, who is our science teacher, introduced the visiting speakers.
Ms. Alvarez, our science teacher, introduced the visiting speakers.
Ms. Alvarez, our science teacher, which introduced the visiting speakers.
questions.explanation: The commas set off a nonrestrictive appositive that identifies Ms. Alvarez without creating a separate clause.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly inverts a past conditional clause while preserving the counterfactual meaning that earlier knowledge would have produced an earlier arrival?
choices: If the team had known about the delay, they would have arrived earlier.
Had the team known about the delay, they would have arrived earlier.
Had the team known about the delay, they would arrive earlier.
The team had known about the delay, and they would have arrived earlier.
questions.explanation: This inversion places the had-clause first and uses would have plus a past participle to express the counterfactual condition accurately.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Maya checked the map twice before she chose the correct trail. Which revision uses a fronted participial phrase to show that the map-checking happened first?
choices: Having checked the map twice, Maya chose the correct trail.
Checked the map twice, Maya chose the correct trail.
Before checking the map twice, Maya chose the correct trail.
After checking the map twice, Maya chose the correct trail.
questions.explanation: Having checked the map twice is a fronted participial phrase that makes the map-checking precede Maya's choice of the trail.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The editor suggested that the writer revises the ending. Which revision correctly uses the subjunctive?
choices: The editor suggested that the writer revise the ending.
The editor suggested that the writer is revising the ending.
The editor suggested that the writer would revise the ending.
The editor suggested that the writer revised the ending.
questions.explanation: The base form revise is the subjunctive used after suggested, meaning the editor advised the writer to change the ending.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The museum, founded in 1890, houses a collection of photographs from the local area. Which explanation best describes the sentence's structure and meaning in plain language?
choices: The phrase founded in 1890 is a prepositional phrase identifying where the collection of photographs was housed.
The phrase founded in 1890 modifies houses and means the museum was founded while it displayed photographs from the local area.
The phrase founded in 1890 is a separate sentence that says the local photographs established the museum in 1890.
The phrase founded in 1890 expands to which was founded and modifies museum, which now contains photographs from the local area.
questions.explanation: The phrase founded in 1890 is a nonrestrictive reduced relative modifying museum, and the sentence says that the museum now contains photographs from the local area.
questions.skill: Explaining advanced syntax in plain language
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision replaces the ambiguous it with a clear noun phrase naming what requires the balancing?
choices: Choosing a teammate can be difficult because the teammate requires balancing skill and cooperation.
Choosing a teammate can be difficult because it requires balancing skill and cooperation.
Choosing a teammate can be difficult because they require balancing skill and cooperation.
Choosing a teammate can be difficult because the decision requires balancing skill and cooperation.
questions.explanation: Naming the decision as the thing that requires balancing gives the reader a clear reference instead of an ambiguous pronoun.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Swimming in cold water was the way that helped Mateo to build endurance. Which revision uses a gerund phrase as the subject while removing unnecessary wording?
choices: Swimming in cold water helped Mateo build endurance.
To swim in cold water helped Mateo build endurance.
Swam in cold water helped Mateo build endurance.
Swimming in cold water was the way that helped Mateo to build endurance.
questions.explanation: The gerund phrase Swimming in cold water functions as the subject, and the revised sentence expresses the original cause-and-effect relationship directly.
questions.skill: Revising a sentence with a gerund-phrase subject
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The library closes at eight, and students must return books before then. Which revision uses a fronted dependent clause to show the time limit without changing the meaning?
choices: Before the library closes at eight, it must return all books.
After students return books, before the library closes at eight, they may leave.
While the library closes at eight, students must return books before then.
Before the library closes at eight, students must return books.
questions.explanation: The fronted dependent clause Before the library closes at eight establishes the deadline before the independent clause.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The club meets online on Mondays, but in person on Thursdays. Which revision uses whereas to create a clear contrast between the two meeting arrangements?
choices: The club meets online on Mondays, whereas it meets in person on Thursdays.
The club meets online on Mondays, where it meets in person on Thursdays.
The club meets online on Mondays, and it meets in person on Thursdays.
The club meets online on Mondays, so it meets in person on Thursdays.
questions.explanation: Whereas contrasts the online meeting on Mondays with the in-person meeting on Thursdays.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The hikers were cold and frightened. The rescuers were warm and calm. Which revision combines the two observations in one balanced compound sentence without adding a causal, temporal, or contrastive connection that the original does not state?
choices: Although the hikers were cold and frightened, the rescuers were warm and calm.
The hikers were cold and frightened, but the rescuers were warm and calm.
The hikers were cold and frightened while the rescuers were warm and calm.
The hikers were cold and frightened, and the rescuers were warm and calm.
questions.explanation: This compound sentence uses the repeated be + adjective + adjective pattern in coordinated independent clauses, creating balance without introducing a new causal, temporal, or contrastive relationship.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The mayor spoke to one candidate about the budget, and that candidate received an award. Which revision uses the formal construction in which a preposition appears immediately before the relative pronoun?
choices: The candidate to who the mayor spoke about the budget received an award.
The candidate which the mayor spoke to about the budget received an award.
The candidate of whom the mayor spoke to about the budget received an award.
The candidate to whom the mayor spoke about the budget received an award.
questions.explanation: The compound relative to whom places the preposition directly before the object pronoun whom and functions as the object of spoke.
questions.skill: Using formal prepositions with relative pronouns
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Some students joined the debate team because they enjoy public speaking, while others joined because they want to improve their confidence. Which revision uses whereas specifically to express contrast and keeps both reasons parallel?
choices: Some students joined the debate team because they enjoy public speaking, while others want to improve their confidence.
Some students joined the debate team because they enjoy public speaking, whereas others joined because they want to improve their confidence.
Some students joined the debate team because they enjoy public speaking, and others joined because they want to improve their confidence.
Some students joined the debate team because they enjoy public speaking, whereas others joined to improve their confidence.
questions.explanation: Whereas introduces a contrasting dependent clause, and the revision uses parallel because clauses to state both groups’ reasons for joining.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly embeds a yes-or-no question within a reporting clause?
choices: The manager asked if the project could be completed on time?
The manager asked whether the project could be completed on time.
The manager asked, if the project could be completed on time.
The manager asked that the project could be completed on time.
questions.explanation: An embedded yes-or-no question uses whether and takes a statement ending in a period rather than a question mark.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Robots are useful in factories, which move heavy parts. Which revision uses a relative adverb to make the location relationship explicit?
choices: Robots are useful in factories, who move heavy parts.
Robots are useful in factories, when they move heavy parts.
Robots are useful in factories, where they move heavy parts.
Robots are useful in factories, whose move heavy parts.
questions.explanation: The relative adverb where correctly indicates that the robots move heavy parts inside the factories.
questions.skill: Revise relative clauses with logical connectors
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The roads had become icy, so the coach sent the players home early after practice. Which revision creates a periodic sentence by placing the dependent clause after the main clause?
choices: Because the roads had become icy, the coach sent the players home early after practice.
The coach sent the players home early after practice because the roads had become icy.
The roads had become icy, and the coach sent the players home early after practice.
The coach sent the players home early after practice, and the roads had become icy.
questions.explanation: The main clause comes first, and the dependent because clause comes last, creating a periodic sentence.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Leo went to the fair. He bought a ticket there. He tried the Ferris wheel. He won a stuffed bear. Which revision presents a main clause and then layers the later actions into an expanding cumulative structure, keeping the actions in chronological order?
choices: Leo went to the fair, where he bought a ticket, tried the Ferris wheel, and won a stuffed bear.
Leo bought a ticket at the fair before he tried the Ferris wheel, and he won a stuffed bear afterward.
Leo won a stuffed bear at the fair after he had bought a ticket and tried the Ferris wheel.
After going to the fair and buying a ticket, Leo tried the Ferris wheel and won a stuffed bear.
questions.explanation: The main clause introduces Leo's trip, and the where clause adds the ticket, ride, and prize as a chronological series of parallel actions.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The longer the musician practiced, the more confident the performance became. Which revision correctly uses the comparative correlative construction the more...the more?
choices: The longer the musician practiced, the performance became the steadier.
The longer the musician practiced, the steadier the performance became.
The musician practiced the longer, the steadier the performance became.
More the musician practiced, the steadier the performance became.
questions.explanation: The paired the more clauses show that the performance became steadier as the musician practiced longer.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The audience was surprised when the final results became available. Which revision uses a that-clause as the subject of the main verb?
choices: It surprised the audience that the final results were available.
The audience was surprised that the final results were available.
That the final results were available surprised the audience.
The final results were available, which surprised the audience.
questions.explanation: The entire clause That the final results were available functions as the subject of surprised.
questions.skill: Using a that-clause as the subject
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The exhibition was postponed because a delivery truck blocked the loading entrance. Which revision correctly forms a reason cleft with a that-clause?
choices: The reason the exhibition was postponed was because a delivery truck blocked the loading entrance.
The reason the exhibition was postponed was that a delivery truck blocked the loading entrance.
The reason the exhibition was postponed was a delivery truck that blocked the loading entrance.
The reason the exhibition was postponed was a delivery truck blocking the loading entrance.
questions.explanation: The standard reason-cleft pattern is The reason ... was that ..., with that introducing the explanatory clause.
questions.skill: Building a reason cleft with a that-clause
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The match began on time despite of the heavy rain. Which revision corrects the preposition error without changing the meaning?
choices: Although the heavy rain, the match began on time.
Despite the heavy rain, the match began on time.
Despite of the rain that was heavy, the match began on time.
Despite the rain was heavy, the match began on time.
questions.explanation: Despite is followed by the noun phrase the heavy rain, and the revision means the match began even though the rain was heavy.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: After the storm passed, the crew reopened the trail. Because visibility improved, hikers returned later that day. Which revision creates two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction, with one dependent clause modifying each independent clause?
choices: After the storm passed, the crew reopened the trail; because visibility improved, hikers returned later that day.
After the storm passed, the crew reopened the trail, and visibility improved because hikers returned later that day.
After the storm passed and because visibility improved, the crew reopened the trail, and hikers returned later that day.
After the storm passed, the crew reopened the trail, and because visibility improved, hikers returned later that day.
questions.explanation: The revision joins two independent clauses with and, while each independent clause contains its own dependent clause.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The final rehearsal helped the actors feel ready for opening night. Which revision uses an it-cleft to emphasize the rehearsal as the cause of the actors' readiness?
choices: It was the actors who felt ready for opening night after the final rehearsal.
It was the final rehearsal that helped the actors feel ready for opening night.
What helped the actors feel ready for opening night was their final rehearsal.
The final rehearsal was what helped the actors feel ready for opening night.
questions.explanation: The it-cleft structure It was the final rehearsal that emphasizes the rehearsal as the cause of the actors' readiness.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Neither the missing permit nor the delayed inspection were enough to prevent the concert from starting. Which revision correctly maintains subject-verb agreement after neither...nor?
choices: Neither the missing permit nor the delayed inspection was enough to prevent the concert from starting.
Neither the missing permit nor the delayed inspection were enough to prevent the concert from starting.
Neither the missing permit nor the delayed inspection were enough to preventing the concert from starting.
Neither the missing permit nor the delayed inspection were enough for preventing the concert from starting.
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, which is the singular delayed inspection here.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision uses an absolute construction to show an accompanying circumstance?
choices: While the child's laughter echoed through the room, the teacher paused to listen.
Because the child's laughter echoed through the room, the teacher paused to listen.
With the child's laughter echoing through the room, the teacher paused to listen.
The child's laughter echoed through the room, and the teacher paused to listen.
questions.explanation: With the child's laughter echoing through the room is an absolute construction that supplies the accompanying circumstance.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision keeps the three items in a grammatically parallel structure?
choices: She reviewed the draft, correcting the errors, and submitted it.
She reviewed the draft, corrected the errors, and submitted it.
She reviewed the draft, corrected the errors, and was submitting it.
She reviewed the draft, to correct the errors, and submitted it.
questions.explanation: The three verbs share the same tense and grammatical form, so the series is parallel.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The students left the gym only after the final bell rang. Which revision correctly fronted a negative adverbial and inverted the subject and auxiliary?
choices: Not until the final bell rang did the students leave the gym.
Not until the final bell rang the students left the gym.
Not until did the final bell ring the students leave the gym.
Not until the final bell rang did the students left the gym.
questions.explanation: Fronting the negative adverbial Not until requires subject-auxiliary inversion, producing did the students leave.
questions.skill: Inverting a sentence after a negative adverbial
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses inversion for emphasis after a negative introductory adverb?
choices: Rarely the committee had approved a proposal so quickly.
Rarely did the committee approved a proposal so quickly.
Rarely had the committee approved a proposal so quickly.
Rarely had the committee approve a proposal so quickly.
questions.explanation: When a negative adverbial such as rarely comes first, subject-auxiliary inversion is required, and had approved is the matching form.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly limits students with an unpunctuated restrictive clause?
choices: Only students who submit essays by Friday qualify for the workshop.
Only students who submit essays by Friday qualify, for the workshop.
Students who submit essays by Friday only qualify for the workshop.
Students, who submit essays by Friday, qualify for the workshop.
questions.explanation: Placing Only before students and leaving the restrictive clause unpunctuated limits the group to those who submit essays by Friday.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The coach's decision after months of debate was fair. Which revision correctly uses a pair of em dashes to set off an interrupting phrase?
choices: The coach's decision, after months of debate—was fair.
The coach's decision—after months of debate, was fair.
The coach's decision—after months of debate—was fair.
The coach's decision—after months of debate was fair.
questions.explanation: A matching pair of em dashes correctly sets off after months of debate as an interruption within the sentence.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Do you mind opening the window? The speaker intends to request permission to perform the action now. Which revision uses a conditional clause to make that request?
choices: Do you mind to open the window now?
Do you mind me opening the window now?
Do you mind my opening the window now?
Do you mind if I open the window now?
questions.explanation: The if-clause if I open the window now directly presents the action as a present-time request for permission.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The scholarship is open to anyone who applies by May 1. Which revision replaces the restrictive relative clause with a correctly formed fused relative clause?
choices: The scholarship is open to whoever will applies by May 1.
The scholarship is open to whomever applies by May 1.
The scholarship is open to whoever applies by May 1.
The scholarship is open to whomever will apply by May 1.
questions.explanation: Whoever is correct because it serves as the subject of applies within the fused relative clause.
questions.skill: Revising restrictive relative clauses into fused relative clauses
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision uses a semicolon to join two closely related independent clauses?
choices: The team practiced until sunset; after a short break, they won the match.
The team practiced until sunset, and then they won the match.
The team practiced until sunset because they wanted to win the match.
The team practiced until sunset, however, and they won the match.
questions.explanation: The semicolon joins two independent clauses, while the comma after the introductory phrase makes the second clause's timing clear.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The guard checked the lobby, switched off the lights, and locked the entrance after the museum closed. Which revision rearranges the sentence into a periodic structure, ending with the main clause?
choices: When the museum closed, the guard checked the lobby, switched off the lights, and locked the entrance.
The guard was checking the lobby, switching off the lights, and locking the entrance when the museum closed.
The guard checked the lobby, switched off the lights, and locked the entrance when the museum closed.
The guard checked the lobby, and the lights were switched off, and the entrance was locked when the museum closed.
questions.explanation: Beginning with the dependent clause When the museum closed places the compound main clause last and creates a periodic structure.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The director encouraged the cast to revise the script. Which revision correctly uses an infinitive clause to complete the verb encouraged?
choices: The director encouraged the cast revising the script.
The director encouraged the cast that revise the script.
The director encouraged the cast to revise the script.
The director encouraged the cast if they revise the script.
questions.explanation: An infinitive clause beginning with to states the action the director encouraged the cast to perform.
questions.skill: Revising a sentence with an infinitive complement
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision makes both the analyzing and the concluding active while preserving the original cause-and-effect relationship?
choices: Because the data were carefully analyzed, a clear conclusion was reached by the research team.
The research team reached a clear conclusion because the data were carefully analyzed.
After the data were carefully analyzed, a clear conclusion was reached by the research team.
Because the research team carefully analyzed the data, it reached a clear conclusion.
questions.explanation: The revision makes the research team the active subject of both actions and retains because to express the original cause-and-effect relationship.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The sun melted the ice into a small pool. Which revision uses the causative pattern caused plus an object and a to-infinitive?
choices: The sun caused the ice to melt into a small pool.
The sun made the ice to melt into a small pool.
The sun had the ice melt into a small pool.
The sun let the ice melt into a small pool.
questions.explanation: The causative construction caused the ice to melt presents the sun as the cause of the ice melting.
questions.skill: Revise causal relationships with causative constructions
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: You may enter the lab only if you wear a badge. Which revision preserves that condition using a single subordinate clause?
choices: You may enter the lab while you are wearing a badge.
You may enter the lab because you wear a badge.
You may enter the lab provided that you wear a badge.
You may enter the lab even though you wear a badge.
questions.explanation: Provided that introduces a condition, so the revision says entry is allowed only when a badge is worn.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The librarian created a display to show how local history shapes neighborhoods. Which revision uses a fronted infinitive phrase to express the purpose while keeping the librarian as the subject?
choices: Showing how local history shapes neighborhoods, the librarian created a display.
For the librarian to show how local history shapes neighborhoods, a display was created.
To show how local history shapes neighborhoods, the librarian's display was created.
To show how local history shapes neighborhoods, the librarian created a display.
questions.explanation: The fronted infinitive states the purpose of creating the display, and the main clause correctly keeps the librarian as the subject.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The judges heard that the singer was repeating the final note. Which revision correctly uses a bare infinitive after the perception verb heard?
choices: The judges heard that the singer repeat the final note.
The judges heard the singer to repeat the final note.
The judges heard the singer repeating the final note.
The judges heard the singer repeat the final note.
questions.explanation: After a perception verb such as heard, the object can be followed by a bare infinitive, here repeat.
questions.skill: Using bare infinitives after perception verbs
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Three problems delayed the launch. The battery overheated, the brakes needed adjustment, and the software crashed. Which revision uses a colon and preserves all three facts exactly?
choices: Three problems delayed the launch: the battery overheated, the brakes needed adjustment, and, the software crashed.
Three problems delayed the launch: the battery overheated, the brakes needed adjustment, and the software crashed.
Three problems delayed the launch: the battery overheated, the brakes needed adjustment, and the software crashed on the runway.
Three problems delayed the launch: the battery overheated, the brakes needed adjustment, and the software crashed the system.
questions.explanation: The colon introduces three parallel clauses that accurately identify the battery, brakes, and software as the causes of the delay.
questions.skill: Revising a sentence with a colon
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The volunteers wanted to finish the trail, but they stopped when it became unsafe. Which revision uses the concessive construction much as while preserving the contrast?
choices: Much as the volunteers finished the trail, they stopped when it became unsafe.
Much the volunteers wanted to finish the trail, they stopped when it became unsafe.
As much the volunteers wanted to finish the trail, they stopped when it became unsafe.
Much as the volunteers wanted to finish the trail, they stopped when it became unsafe.
questions.explanation: Much as introduces the volunteers' concession before the contrasting main clause about their stopping.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The storm damaged the cabin's roof. Which revision uses a wh-cleft to emphasize the part of the cabin that was damaged?
choices: The storm damaged what the roof was.
The cabin's roof was what the storm damaged was.
What damaged the storm was the cabin's roof.
What the storm damaged was the cabin's roof.
questions.explanation: Placing What the storm damaged in the opening clause makes the damaged object the emphatic focus of the sentence.
questions.skill: Revising a sentence with a wh-cleft
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: A long delay kept the team from arriving on time. Which revision uses an existential there construction without making the cause vague?
choices: It was a long delay that kept the team from arriving on time.
A long delay was there that kept the team from arriving on time.
There was a long delay that kept the team from arriving on time.
There had a long delay that kept the team from arriving on time.
questions.explanation: The existential phrase There was introduces the delay, while the relative clause identifies what it caused.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Ms. Imani was very busy preparing the exhibit that she forgot the submission deadline. Which revision uses the so-that result pattern correctly?
choices: Ms. Imani was too busy preparing the exhibit to forget the submission deadline.
Ms. Imani was so busy preparing the exhibit that she forgot the submission deadline.
Ms. Imani was such busy preparing the exhibit that she forgot the submission deadline.
Ms. Imani was very busy preparing the exhibit so that she forgot the submission deadline.
questions.explanation: The correlative pair so and that correctly connects the intensity of Ms. Imani’s busyness to the result that she forgot the deadline.
questions.skill: Revise result relationships with correlative conjunctions
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: Which revision best preserves the intended cause-and-effect relationship in the original sentence: The plants survived because the class watered them?
choices: Because the class watered the plants, the plants survived.
Although the class watered the plants, the plants survived.
The plants survived, but the class watered the plants.
The class watered the plants whenever the plants survived.
questions.explanation: The because clause identifies the class's watering as the cause of the plants' survival.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

questions.prompt: The editor reread the final paragraph carefully so that no names would be misspelled. Which revision uses a lest clause to express the same concern about avoiding errors?
choices: The editor reread the final paragraph carefully so that a name would be misspelled.
The editor reread the final paragraph carefully lest a name be misspelled.
The editor reread the final paragraph carefully lest a name would be misspelled.
The editor reread the final paragraph carefully so that no name be misspelled.
questions.explanation: A lest clause introduces a feared outcome and conventionally takes the bare subjunctive form be.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

feedback.correct: Sharp revision — that sentence now works on purpose.
feedback.incorrect: Half the pot gone. Next flip is a fresh sentence.
feedback.win: One hundred points! You revise sentences like a craftsperson, not a patcher.
feedback.lose: The pot ran dry. A weak sentence beat you — try another run.

kept.prompt: Which revision uses a semicolon to join two closely related independent clauses?
choices: The team practiced until sunset, and then they won the match.
The team practiced until sunset; after a short break, they won the match.
The team practiced until sunset because they wanted to win the match.
The team practiced until sunset, however, and they won the match.
kept.explanation: The semicolon joins two independent clauses, while the comma after the introductory phrase makes the second clause's timing clear.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision keeps the three items in a grammatically parallel structure?
choices: She reviewed the draft, corrected the errors, and submitted it.
She reviewed the draft, correcting the errors, and submitted it.
She reviewed the draft, corrected the errors, and was submitting it.
She reviewed the draft, to correct the errors, and submitted it.
kept.explanation: The three verbs share the same tense and grammatical form, so the series is parallel.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision correctly uses a nonrestrictive appositive to identify Ms. Alvarez?
choices: Ms. Alvarez, our science teacher, introduced the visiting speakers.
Ms. Alvarez, who is our science teacher, introduced the visiting speakers.
Ms. Alvarez, our science teacher introduced the visiting speakers.
Ms. Alvarez, our science teacher, which introduced the visiting speakers.
kept.explanation: The commas set off a nonrestrictive appositive that identifies Ms. Alvarez without creating a separate clause.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision replaces the ambiguous it with a clear noun phrase naming what requires the balancing?
choices: Choosing a teammate can be difficult because the decision requires balancing skill and cooperation.
Choosing a teammate can be difficult because it requires balancing skill and cooperation.
Choosing a teammate can be difficult because they require balancing skill and cooperation.
Choosing a teammate can be difficult because the teammate requires balancing skill and cooperation.
kept.explanation: Naming the decision as the thing that requires balancing gives the reader a clear reference instead of an ambiguous pronoun.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision best preserves the intended cause-and-effect relationship in the original sentence: The plants survived because the class watered them?
choices: Because the class watered the plants, the plants survived.
Although the class watered the plants, the plants survived.
The plants survived, but the class watered the plants.
The class watered the plants whenever the plants survived.
kept.explanation: The because clause identifies the class's watering as the cause of the plants' survival.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision uses one introductory dependent clause followed by one independent clause?
choices: The runners completed the relay before dusk, although the rain delayed the start.
The rain delayed the start, and the runners completed the relay before dusk.
Although the rain delayed the start, the runners completed the relay before dusk.
Although the rain delayed the start, and because the team wanted to win, they completed the relay.
kept.explanation: The revision places one dependent although-clause before one independent clause, the structure the prompt asks for.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision uses an absolute construction to show an accompanying circumstance?
choices: While the child's laughter echoed through the room, the teacher paused to listen.
Because the child's laughter echoed through the room, the teacher paused to listen.
The child's laughter echoed through the room, and the teacher paused to listen.
With the child's laughter echoing through the room, the teacher paused to listen.
kept.explanation: With the child's laughter echoing through the room is an absolute construction that supplies the accompanying circumstance.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision makes both the analyzing and the concluding active while preserving the original cause-and-effect relationship?
choices: Because the data were carefully analyzed, a clear conclusion was reached by the research team.
Because the research team carefully analyzed the data, it reached a clear conclusion.
After the data were carefully analyzed, a clear conclusion was reached by the research team.
The research team reached a clear conclusion because the data were carefully analyzed.
kept.explanation: The revision makes the research team the active subject of both actions and retains because to express the original cause-and-effect relationship.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision correctly limits students with an unpunctuated restrictive clause?
choices: Only students who submit essays by Friday qualify for the workshop.
Only students who submit essays by Friday qualify, for the workshop.
Students who submit essays by Friday only qualify for the workshop.
Students, who submit essays by Friday, qualify for the workshop.
kept.explanation: Placing Only before students and leaving the restrictive clause unpunctuated limits the group to those who submit essays by Friday.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision correctly embeds a yes-or-no question within a reporting clause?
choices: The manager asked if the project could be completed on time?
The manager asked, if the project could be completed on time.
The manager asked whether the project could be completed on time.
The manager asked that the project could be completed on time.
kept.explanation: An embedded yes-or-no question uses whether and takes a statement ending in a period rather than a question mark.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision correctly uses inversion for emphasis after a negative introductory adverb?
choices: Rarely the committee had approved a proposal so quickly.
Rarely did the committee approved a proposal so quickly.
Rarely had the committee approve a proposal so quickly.
Rarely had the committee approved a proposal so quickly.
kept.explanation: When a negative adverbial such as rarely comes first, subject-auxiliary inversion is required, and had approved is the matching form.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The hikers were cold and frightened. The rescuers were warm and calm. Which revision combines the two observations in one balanced compound sentence without adding a causal, temporal, or contrastive connection that the original does not state?
choices: Although the hikers were cold and frightened, the rescuers were warm and calm.
The hikers were cold and frightened, and the rescuers were warm and calm.
The hikers were cold and frightened while the rescuers were warm and calm.
The hikers were cold and frightened, but the rescuers were warm and calm.
kept.explanation: This compound sentence uses the repeated be + adjective + adjective pattern in coordinated independent clauses, creating balance without introducing a new causal, temporal, or contrastive relationship.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Leo went to the fair. He bought a ticket there. He tried the Ferris wheel. He won a stuffed bear. Which revision presents a main clause and then layers the later actions into an expanding cumulative structure, keeping the actions in chronological order?
choices: After going to the fair and buying a ticket, Leo tried the Ferris wheel and won a stuffed bear.
Leo bought a ticket at the fair before he tried the Ferris wheel, and he won a stuffed bear afterward.
Leo won a stuffed bear at the fair after he had bought a ticket and tried the Ferris wheel.
Leo went to the fair, where he bought a ticket, tried the Ferris wheel, and won a stuffed bear.
kept.explanation: The main clause introduces Leo's trip, and the where clause adds the ticket, ride, and prize as a chronological series of parallel actions.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision correctly inverts a past conditional clause while preserving the counterfactual meaning that earlier knowledge would have produced an earlier arrival?
choices: If the team had known about the delay, they would have arrived earlier.
Had the team known about the delay, they would arrive earlier.
Had the team known about the delay, they would have arrived earlier.
The team had known about the delay, and they would have arrived earlier.
kept.explanation: This inversion places the had-clause first and uses would have plus a past participle to express the counterfactual condition accurately.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Which revision correctly uses not only...but also while keeping the subject in place and giving each half one simple-past active verb?
choices: Not only did the interns catalog every sample, but they also recorded each test result carefully.
The interns not only cataloged and recorded every sample but also filed each test result carefully.
The interns not only cataloged every sample but also were recording each test result carefully.
The interns not only cataloged every sample but also recorded each test result carefully.
kept.explanation: This construction keeps the interns as the subject and uses one active simple-past verb in each half, so the two actions remain parallel.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The librarian created a display to show how local history shapes neighborhoods. Which revision uses a fronted infinitive phrase to express the purpose while keeping the librarian as the subject?
choices: Showing how local history shapes neighborhoods, the librarian created a display.
For the librarian to show how local history shapes neighborhoods, a display was created.
To show how local history shapes neighborhoods, the librarian created a display.
To show how local history shapes neighborhoods, the librarian's display was created.
kept.explanation: The fronted infinitive states the purpose of creating the display, and the main clause correctly keeps the librarian as the subject.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Maya checked the map twice before she chose the correct trail. Which revision uses a fronted participial phrase to show that the map-checking happened first?
choices: Having checked the map twice, Maya chose the correct trail.
Checked the map twice, Maya chose the correct trail.
Before checking the map twice, Maya chose the correct trail.
After checking the map twice, Maya chose the correct trail.
kept.explanation: Having checked the map twice is a fronted participial phrase that makes the map-checking precede Maya's choice of the trail.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The final rehearsal helped the actors feel ready for opening night. Which revision uses an it-cleft to emphasize the rehearsal as the cause of the actors' readiness?
choices: It was the final rehearsal that helped the actors feel ready for opening night.
It was the actors who felt ready for opening night after the final rehearsal.
What helped the actors feel ready for opening night was their final rehearsal.
The final rehearsal was what helped the actors feel ready for opening night.
kept.explanation: The it-cleft structure It was the final rehearsal that emphasizes the rehearsal as the cause of the actors' readiness.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The bicycle repair shop stays open until six. It is located on Pine Street. Which revision correctly places a nonrestrictive relative clause immediately after its antecedent to add the location as extra information?
choices: The bicycle repair shop, which is located on Pine Street, stays open until six.
The bicycle repair shop on Pine Street stays open until six.
The bicycle repair shop stays open until six, which is located on Pine Street.
The bicycle repair shop, located on Pine Street, stays open until six.
kept.explanation: The nonrestrictive relative clause which is located on Pine Street directly follows and modifies bicycle repair shop and is correctly set off by commas.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The museum, founded in 1890, houses a collection of photographs from the local area. Which explanation best describes the sentence's structure and meaning in plain language?
choices: The phrase founded in 1890 expands to which was founded and modifies museum, which now contains photographs from the local area.
The phrase founded in 1890 modifies houses and means the museum was founded while it displayed photographs from the local area.
The phrase founded in 1890 is a separate sentence that says the local photographs established the museum in 1890.
The phrase founded in 1890 is a prepositional phrase identifying where the collection of photographs was housed.
kept.explanation: The phrase founded in 1890 is a nonrestrictive reduced relative modifying museum, and the sentence says that the museum now contains photographs from the local area.
kept.skill: Explaining advanced syntax in plain language
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The editor suggested that the writer revises the ending. Which revision correctly uses the subjunctive?
choices: The editor suggested that the writer revise the ending.
The editor suggested that the writer is revising the ending.
The editor suggested that the writer would revise the ending.
The editor suggested that the writer revised the ending.
kept.explanation: The base form revise is the subjunctive used after suggested, meaning the editor advised the writer to change the ending.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The match began on time despite of the heavy rain. Which revision corrects the preposition error without changing the meaning?
choices: Despite the heavy rain, the match began on time.
Although the heavy rain, the match began on time.
Despite of the rain that was heavy, the match began on time.
Despite the rain was heavy, the match began on time.
kept.explanation: Despite is followed by the noun phrase the heavy rain, and the revision means the match began even though the rain was heavy.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: You may enter the lab only if you wear a badge. Which revision preserves that condition using a single subordinate clause?
choices: You may enter the lab provided that you wear a badge.
You may enter the lab because you wear a badge.
You may enter the lab while you are wearing a badge.
You may enter the lab even though you wear a badge.
kept.explanation: Provided that introduces a condition, so the revision says entry is allowed only when a badge is worn.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: After the storm passed, the crew reopened the trail. Because visibility improved, hikers returned later that day. Which revision creates two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction, with one dependent clause modifying each independent clause?
choices: After the storm passed, the crew reopened the trail, and because visibility improved, hikers returned later that day.
After the storm passed, the crew reopened the trail, and visibility improved because hikers returned later that day.
After the storm passed and because visibility improved, the crew reopened the trail, and hikers returned later that day.
After the storm passed, the crew reopened the trail; because visibility improved, hikers returned later that day.
kept.explanation: The revision joins two independent clauses with and, while each independent clause contains its own dependent clause.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The coach would rather revising the plan than presenting it. Which revision uses parallel infinitives after would rather?
choices: The coach would rather revise the plan than present it.
The coach would rather to revise the plan than present it.
The coach would rather revise the plan than to present it.
The coach would rather revising the plan than present it.
kept.explanation: Would rather is followed by the parallel infinitives revise and present, which clearly express the coach's preference.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The longer the musician practiced, the more confident the performance became. Which revision correctly uses the comparative correlative construction the more...the more?
choices: The longer the musician practiced, the steadier the performance became.
The longer the musician practiced, the performance became the steadier.
The musician practiced the longer, the steadier the performance became.
More the musician practiced, the steadier the performance became.
kept.explanation: The paired the more clauses show that the performance became steadier as the musician practiced longer.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The scholarship is open to anyone who applies by May 1. Which revision replaces the restrictive relative clause with a correctly formed fused relative clause?
choices: The scholarship is open to whoever applies by May 1.
The scholarship is open to whomever applies by May 1.
The scholarship is open to whoever will applies by May 1.
The scholarship is open to whomever will apply by May 1.
kept.explanation: Whoever is correct because it serves as the subject of applies within the fused relative clause.
kept.skill: Revising restrictive relative clauses into fused relative clauses
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The storm damaged the cabin's roof. Which revision uses a wh-cleft to emphasize the part of the cabin that was damaged?
choices: The storm damaged what the roof was.
What the storm damaged was the cabin's roof.

The cabin's roof was what the storm damaged was.
kept.explanation: Placing What the storm damaged in the opening clause makes the damaged object the emphatic focus of the sentence.
kept.skill: Revising a sentence with a wh-cleft
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Swimming in cold water was the way that helped Mateo to build endurance. Which revision uses a gerund phrase as the subject while removing unnecessary wording?
choices: Swimming in cold water helped Mateo build endurance.
To swim in cold water helped Mateo build endurance.
Swam in cold water helped Mateo build endurance.
Swimming in cold water was the way that helped Mateo to build endurance.
kept.explanation: The gerund phrase Swimming in cold water functions as the subject, and the revised sentence expresses the original cause-and-effect relationship directly.
kept.skill: Revising a sentence with a gerund-phrase subject
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Three problems delayed the launch. The battery overheated, the brakes needed adjustment, and the software crashed. Which revision uses a colon and preserves all three facts exactly?
choices: Three problems delayed the launch: the battery overheated, the brakes needed adjustment, and the software crashed.
Three problems delayed the launch: the battery overheated, the brakes needed adjustment, and, the software crashed.
Three problems delayed the launch: the battery overheated, the brakes needed adjustment, and the software crashed on the runway.
Three problems delayed the launch: the battery overheated, the brakes needed adjustment, and the software crashed the system.
kept.explanation: The colon introduces three parallel clauses that accurately identify the battery, brakes, and software as the causes of the delay.
kept.skill: Revising a sentence with a colon
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The director encouraged the cast to revise the script. Which revision correctly uses an infinitive clause to complete the verb encouraged?
choices: The director encouraged the cast revising the script.
The director encouraged the cast that revise the script.
The director encouraged the cast if they revise the script.
The director encouraged the cast to revise the script.

kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The mayor spoke to one candidate about the budget, and that candidate received an award. Which revision uses the formal construction in which a preposition appears immediately before the relative pronoun?
choices: The candidate to who the mayor spoke about the budget received an award.
The candidate which the mayor spoke to about the budget received an award.
The candidate to whom the mayor spoke about the budget received an award.
The candidate of whom the mayor spoke to about the budget received an award.
kept.explanation: The compound relative to whom places the preposition directly before the object pronoun whom and functions as the object of spoke.
kept.skill: Using formal prepositions with relative pronouns
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The students left the gym only after the final bell rang. Which revision correctly fronted a negative adverbial and inverted the subject and auxiliary?
choices: Not until the final bell rang the students left the gym.
Not until the final bell rang did the students leave the gym.
Not until did the final bell ring the students leave the gym.
Not until the final bell rang did the students left the gym.
kept.explanation: Fronting the negative adverbial Not until requires subject-auxiliary inversion, producing did the students leave.
kept.skill: Inverting a sentence after a negative adverbial
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The exhibition was postponed because a delivery truck blocked the loading entrance. Which revision correctly forms a reason cleft with a that-clause?
choices: The reason the exhibition was postponed was because a delivery truck blocked the loading entrance.
The reason the exhibition was postponed was a delivery truck blocking the loading entrance.
The reason the exhibition was postponed was a delivery truck that blocked the loading entrance.
The reason the exhibition was postponed was that a delivery truck blocked the loading entrance.
kept.explanation: The standard reason-cleft pattern is The reason ... was that ..., with that introducing the explanatory clause.

kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The audience was surprised when the final results became available. Which revision uses a that-clause as the subject of the main verb?
choices: It surprised the audience that the final results were available.
The audience was surprised that the final results were available.
That the final results were available surprised the audience.
The final results were available, which surprised the audience.
kept.explanation: The entire clause That the final results were available functions as the subject of surprised.
kept.skill: Using a that-clause as the subject
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The judges heard that the singer was repeating the final note. Which revision correctly uses a bare infinitive after the perception verb heard?
choices: The judges heard the singer repeat the final note.
The judges heard the singer to repeat the final note.
The judges heard the singer repeating the final note.
The judges heard that the singer repeat the final note.
kept.explanation: After a perception verb such as heard, the object can be followed by a bare infinitive, here repeat.

kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Neither the missing permit nor the delayed inspection were enough to prevent the concert from starting. Which revision correctly maintains subject-verb agreement after neither...nor?
choices: Neither the missing permit nor the delayed inspection were enough to prevent the concert from starting.
Neither the missing permit nor the delayed inspection was enough to prevent the concert from starting.
Neither the missing permit nor the delayed inspection were enough to preventing the concert from starting.
Neither the missing permit nor the delayed inspection were enough for preventing the concert from starting.
kept.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, which is the singular delayed inspection here.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Some students joined the debate team because they enjoy public speaking, while others joined because they want to improve their confidence. Which revision uses whereas specifically to express contrast and keeps both reasons parallel?
choices: Some students joined the debate team because they enjoy public speaking, whereas others joined because they want to improve their confidence.
Some students joined the debate team because they enjoy public speaking, while others want to improve their confidence.
Some students joined the debate team because they enjoy public speaking, and others joined because they want to improve their confidence.
Some students joined the debate team because they enjoy public speaking, whereas others joined to improve their confidence.
kept.explanation: Whereas introduces a contrasting dependent clause, and the revision uses parallel because clauses to state both groups’ reasons for joining.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Robots are useful in factories, which move heavy parts. Which revision uses a relative adverb to make the location relationship explicit?
choices: Robots are useful in factories, where they move heavy parts.
Robots are useful in factories, when they move heavy parts.
Robots are useful in factories, who move heavy parts.
Robots are useful in factories, whose move heavy parts.
kept.explanation: The relative adverb where correctly indicates that the robots move heavy parts inside the factories.
kept.skill: Revise relative clauses with logical connectors
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Do you mind opening the window? The speaker intends to request permission to perform the action now. Which revision uses a conditional clause to make that request?
choices: Do you mind if I open the window now?
Do you mind me opening the window now?
Do you mind my opening the window now?
Do you mind to open the window now?
kept.explanation: The if-clause if I open the window now directly presents the action as a present-time request for permission.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The sun melted the ice into a small pool. Which revision uses the causative pattern caused plus an object and a to-infinitive?
choices: The sun caused the ice to melt into a small pool.
The sun made the ice to melt into a small pool.
The sun had the ice melt into a small pool.
The sun let the ice melt into a small pool.
kept.explanation: The causative construction caused the ice to melt presents the sun as the cause of the ice melting.
kept.skill: Revise causal relationships with causative constructions
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: Ms. Imani was very busy preparing the exhibit that she forgot the submission deadline. Which revision uses the so-that result pattern correctly?
choices: Ms. Imani was so busy preparing the exhibit that she forgot the submission deadline.
Ms. Imani was too busy preparing the exhibit to forget the submission deadline.
Ms. Imani was such busy preparing the exhibit that she forgot the submission deadline.
Ms. Imani was very busy preparing the exhibit so that she forgot the submission deadline.
kept.explanation: The correlative pair so and that correctly connects the intensity of Ms. Imani’s busyness to the result that she forgot the deadline.

kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The coach's decision after months of debate was fair. Which revision correctly uses a pair of em dashes to set off an interrupting phrase?

The coach's decision—after months of debate, was fair.
The coach's decision, after months of debate—was fair.
The coach's decision—after months of debate was fair.
kept.explanation: A matching pair of em dashes correctly sets off after months of debate as an interruption within the sentence.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The library closes at eight, and students must return books before then. Which revision uses a fronted dependent clause to show the time limit without changing the meaning?
choices: Before the library closes at eight, students must return books.
After students return books, before the library closes at eight, they may leave.
While the library closes at eight, students must return books before then.
Before the library closes at eight, it must return all books.
kept.explanation: The fronted dependent clause Before the library closes at eight establishes the deadline before the independent clause.

kept.prompt: The guard checked the lobby, switched off the lights, and locked the entrance after the museum closed. Which revision rearranges the sentence into a periodic structure, ending with the main clause?
choices: The guard checked the lobby, switched off the lights, and locked the entrance when the museum closed.
The guard was checking the lobby, switching off the lights, and locking the entrance when the museum closed.
When the museum closed, the guard checked the lobby, switched off the lights, and locked the entrance.
The guard checked the lobby, and the lights were switched off, and the entrance was locked when the museum closed.
kept.explanation: Beginning with the dependent clause When the museum closed places the compound main clause last and creates a periodic structure.
kept.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The editor reread the final paragraph carefully so that no names would be misspelled. Which revision uses a lest clause to express the same concern about avoiding errors?
choices: The editor reread the final paragraph carefully so that a name would be misspelled.
The editor reread the final paragraph carefully lest a name be misspelled.
The editor reread the final paragraph carefully lest a name would be misspelled.
The editor reread the final paragraph carefully so that no name be misspelled.
kept.explanation: A lest clause introduces a feared outcome and conventionally takes the bare subjunctive form be.
kept.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: A long delay kept the team from arriving on time. Which revision uses an existential there construction without making the cause vague?
choices: It was a long delay that kept the team from arriving on time.
A long delay was there that kept the team from arriving on time.
There had a long delay that kept the team from arriving on time.
There was a long delay that kept the team from arriving on time.

kept.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The volunteers wanted to finish the trail, but they stopped when it became unsafe. Which revision uses the concessive construction much as while preserving the contrast?
choices: Much as the volunteers wanted to finish the trail, they stopped when it became unsafe.
Much the volunteers wanted to finish the trail, they stopped when it became unsafe.
As much the volunteers wanted to finish the trail, they stopped when it became unsafe.
Much as the volunteers finished the trail, they stopped when it became unsafe.

kept.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The club meets online on Mondays, but in person on Thursdays. Which revision uses whereas to create a clear contrast between the two meeting arrangements?
choices: The club meets online on Mondays, and it meets in person on Thursdays.
The club meets online on Mondays, where it meets in person on Thursdays.
The club meets online on Mondays, whereas it meets in person on Thursdays.
The club meets online on Mondays, so it meets in person on Thursdays.
kept.explanation: Whereas contrasts the online meeting on Mondays with the in-person meeting on Thursdays.
kept.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Syntax and Sentence Craft

kept.prompt: The roads had become icy, so the coach sent the players home early after practice. Which revision creates a periodic sentence by placing the dependent clause after the main clause?
choices: The coach sent the players home early after practice because the roads had become icy.
Because the roads had become icy, the coach sent the players home early after practice.
The roads had become icy, and the coach sent the players home early after practice.
The coach sent the players home early after practice, and the roads had become icy.

rejected.prompt: Which revision avoids a dangling modifier by placing the introductory phrase next to the person who performs the action?
choices: Opening the door, Lena greeted the waiting visitor.
Opening the door, the waiting visitor greeted Lena.
